# Opteryx

> Opteryx is a SQL query engine for data where it lives: Parquet and other files on disk or in S3 and GCS, Iceberg catalogs, PostgreSQL and Firestore. Opteryx Core is the open-source engine, embedded in Python; Opteryx Studio (opteryx.app) is the hosted platform. Opteryx SQL is close to PostgreSQL but is not the same dialect.

Before writing Opteryx SQL, read the SQL guide for agents. Every example in it is executed against Opteryx Core before it is published.

## SQL guides for agents

- [Opteryx SQL Guide for Agents](https://docs.opteryx.app/opteryx-sql-guide.md): naming datasets, quoting and identifiers, supported statements and functions, differences from PostgreSQL and ANSI SQL, time travel, common errors with fixes, and copy-paste examples (about 5,000 tokens)
- [Opteryx SQL: Short Guide](https://docs.opteryx.app/opteryx-sql-guide-short.md): the same rules condensed to about 1,200 tokens, for small models and system prompts

## Using Opteryx with AI assistants

- [Asking Questions of Local Data with Ollama](https://docs.opteryx.app/docs/guides/local-ai-with-ollama): a local model, a local MCP server and Opteryx Core, with no account and no network
- [Using Opteryx from Your AI Assistant](https://docs.opteryx.app/docs/guides/ai-assistants): the hosted Opteryx MCP server
